newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-MAJOLI SCRAPES INTO WIMBLEDON LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MAJOLI SCRAPES INTO WIMBLEDON LAST EIGHT.

text.p: French open champion Iva Majoli scraped into the Wimbledon quarter-finals by the skin of her teeth after finally sinking Romanian Irina Spirlea on Tuesday.

In a marathon three-set match that was interrupted twice by rain, there was little to separate fourth seed Majoli and Spirlea, seeded number 12. But after a little over two hours, the Croatian finally clinched her place 6-7 (8-10) 6-1 9-7.
In the first set the games went with serve but the Romanian looked the more composed and eventually won after a thrilling tie break.
The gap between the pair in the second set was not as wide as the score suggested, but Spirlea had patches where she could only hit the ball right out of court or into the net.
By the final game, she looked as if she had given up totally -- refusing to run for a low ball and hitting others way out.
Majoli, who has a back injury, became the more aggressive of the two and impressed with some skilful volleying and speed to the net.
Spirlea lost her serve in the first game of the final set, but games then went with serve until the nail-biting 10th, when after six deuces, Spirlea finally broke back with a vicious forehand return.
But her brilliant yet sometimes unreliable forehand let her down, and allowed Majoli to take her serve in the 15th game and then the match.
Afterwards, a relieved Majoli, who until last Tuesday had never won a match on grass, said she was pleased with her game.
"I had a good serve, especially when I needed it. She only broke my serve once," she said.
Her back however is still problematic, despite twice-daily treatment since she put out Briton Karen Cross on Sunday.
"I still don't feel well but when I'm playing it's not so bad as when I'm just standing or sitting," she said.
In the quarter-finals Majoli faces 16-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova who surprisingly knocked out veteran Helena Sukova, but the Croatian is confident.
"I think it's better for me to play Kournikova than Sukova because Sukova is better on grass. I think I have a pretty big chance to win," she said.
